_comment: ADR-037 register fragment — registration forms. Adds the disjoint schema keys `registrationForm` and `formDraft` to the shared `buildiq` register's components.schemas map (key-union merge, no existing schema is touched). A registration form is the manifest form contract bound to one type value of one consuming app's object, and a type carries several of them: one per audience and channel, at most one default each. The form owns its own field order and grouping, so a served form is what an administrator arranged rather than the target schema's property order. Presets let a form decide an answer the filer never sees, and they travel BESIDE the served form: buildiq hands them to the consumer and never writes the consuming app's object itself (ADR-066). See openspec/changes/forms-per-case-type/specs/registration-form-builder/spec.md, REQ-OBRF-004 through REQ-OBRF-009.

registrationForm.title: Registration Form
registrationForm.description: A form bound to one type value of one object in one app: the intake form for a bouwvergunning, the desk form for the same type, the form an architect fills in on a client's behalf. One type carries SEVERAL forms, each named, each for an audience and a channel, and at most one of them is the default for its audience and channel. The form owns the order and the grouping of its fields, so what a filer sees is what an administrator arranged and not whatever order the schema happens to list its properties in.

x-openregister-audit-trail.description: A registration form is what a citizen is asked. Every create, edit and publication is recorded, so what was asked on a given day stays answerable.

name.title: Name
name.description: The form's own name, unique within the type tuple. This is what a consumer asks for by name, so it is stable and an administrator renames it deliberately (REQ-OBRF-004).

audience.title: Audience
audience.description: Who fills this form in: the applicant, a member of staff at the desk, or a professional acting for somebody else. The same case type is asked differently by each (REQ-OBRF-004).

isDefault.title: Is Default
isDefault.description: Whether this is the form a consumer gets when it asks for the audience and channel without naming one. At most one published form per (type tuple, audience, channel) may be the default; a second is refused and names the first (REQ-OBRF-004, REQ-OBRF-007).

channel.title: Channel
channel.description: The intake channel this form serves. Validated against the consuming schema's own channel property where one is declared, so a channel the consumer has never heard of is refused rather than published and never asked for. A form with no channel serves every channel (REQ-OBRF-007).

channelProperty.title: Channel Property
channelProperty.description: The property on the target schema that carries the intake channel, named the same way `typeProperty` names the one carrying the type. Its enum is what a channel is checked against. Buildiq never guesses this from a property name: refusing a save on a name that merely looks channel-ish is a worse failure than not refusing at all. A form that names no channel property is not channel-checked (REQ-OBRF-007).

isPublic.title: Is Public
isPublic.description: Whether the form may be shown to somebody who is not logged in. The portal reads this; buildiq does not serve the form itself (REQ-OBRF-009).

confirmationText.example: Uw aanvraag is ontvangen. U hoort binnen acht weken van ons.
confirmationText.title: Confirmation Text
confirmationText.description: What the filer reads after submitting. Written by the administrator who owns the form, because the sentence that ends an application is part of the application.

targetApp.title: Target App
targetApp.description: The app whose object this form creates.

register.title: Register
register.description: The register slug holding that object.

schema.title: Schema
schema.description: The schema slug of that object.

typeProperty.title: Type Property
typeProperty.description: The property on that schema carrying the type value.

typeValue.title: Type Value
typeValue.description: The type value this form is bound to.

sections.description: The groups the fields are arranged into, in the order an administrator set. A field naming a section that is not declared here is refused on save (REQ-OBRF-008).

name.title: Name
name.description: The section's own name, referenced by fields.

order.title: Order
order.description: Where the section sits on the form.

sections.title: Sections

fields.description: The fields this form asks, with their order and their section. A form lists only the fields an administrator put on it, never every property of the target schema in fetch order.

name.title: Name
name.description: The property on the target schema this field writes.

label.title: Label
label.description: What the filer reads above the input.

type.title: Type
type.description: The input type, as the manifest form contract names it.

required.title: Required
required.description: Whether the filer must answer it.

section.title: Section
section.description: The declared section this field sits in. A section the form does not declare is refused on save (REQ-OBRF-008).

order.title: Order
order.description: Where the field sits inside its section. The served form uses this order and NEVER the schema's property order: a form that fell back to property order would silently reshuffle the day somebody adds a property (REQ-OBRF-008).

default.title: Default
default.description: Pre-filled value. Set by the serving layer from a visible preset; an author sets it directly for a plain default.

fields.title: Fields

steps.description: The manifest form contract's steps, each with a free phase label shown as the group heading.
steps.title: Steps

formLogic.description: The manifest form contract's conditional logic: visibleWhen and validation, authored by the same editor that authors every other manifest form.
formLogic.title: Form Logic

presets.description: Values the form sets on the object it creates. A hidden preset is REMOVED from the served fields and travels beside the form instead, so the filer never sees a question whose answer was already decided; a visible one is pre-filled and stays editable. buildiq never writes the target object: the consumer does, from these (REQ-OBRF-005).

field.title: Field
field.description: The property on the target schema this preset sets.

value.title: Value
value.description: The value it is set to.

hidden.title: Hidden
hidden.description: Whether the filer sees it. Hidden means removed from the form, not merely styled away.

presets.title: Presets

allowSaveForLater.title: Allow Save For Later
allowSaveForLater.description: Whether a filer may save a draft and come back to it.

status.title: Status
status.description: Lifecycle. Only a published form is served to a consumer; a draft is the administrator's working copy.

formDraft.x-openregister-demo-data: One person's half-filled form, owner-only. A generated draft belongs to a user who does not exist, so nobody can ever open it.
formDraft.title: Form Draft
formDraft.description: A half-filled registration form belonging to one person. Owner-only: the values are that person's own answers, often personal data, and nobody else has a reason to read them. Drafts are the one append the leaf allows, because they are buildiq's own data and nothing else's (ADR-066).

x-openregister-audit-trail.description: Draft values are personal data; every write is recorded.

registrationFormId.title: Registration Form Id
registrationFormId.description: The form this draft is an answer to.

userId.title: User Id
userId.description: Whose draft this is. The only person who may read it.

values.description: The answers so far, keyed by field name.
values.title: Values

step.title: Step
step.description: Which step the filer had reached.
